table.name: countries
table.purpose: A lookup table of countries (likely European), one row per country, referenced by other tables such as t03 and t02 via its primary key col_001. The opaque numeric IDs suggest this is a subset or sample of a larger country list (11 rows).

col_001.name: country_id
col_001.description: Primary key: surrogate integer identifier for a country. Referenced by t03 (col_002, col_003) and t02 (col_002).

col_002.name: country_name
col_002.description: Name of the country (e.g. Belgium, England, France, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Portugal, Netherlands, Spain). Unique per row.

table.name: league
table.purpose: Lookup table of football (soccer) leagues; each row is one league with its name and the id of its country. Referenced by t03 (likely matches/teams).

col_001.name: league_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the league table; unique integer id per league.

col_002.name: country_id
col_002.description: Id of the country the league belongs to; references t01.col_001 (country table, whose label column gives names like England, Germany, Portugal).

col_003.name: league_name
col_003.description: Full name of the league, combining country and competition name (e.g. 'England Premier League', 'Germany 1. Bundesliga').

table.name: Match
table.purpose: One row per soccer/football match: teams, date, season, score, lineups, in-match event XML, and pre-match betting odds from multiple bookmakers (this is the 'Match' table of the European Soccer Database).

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Synthetic primary key of the match row (1..25979, unique).

col_002.name: country_id
col_002.description: FK to country table (t01); values resolve to England, Germany, Portugal, Spain, Switzerland, etc.

col_003.name: league_id
col_003.description: FK to league table (t02); values resolve to e.g. England Premier League, Spain LIGA BBVA. Duplicates col_002 values because each league maps 1:1 to a country in this dataset.

col_005.name: stage

table.name: players
table.purpose: Registry of football players with identifiers, full name, date of birth, height and weight. Referenced by statistics tables t03, t05 and t07 (player match/event stats).

col_001.name: player_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the player table; sequential surrogate identifier (1..11075).

col_002.name: player_ref_id
col_002.description: Second unique player identifier (range 2625..750584), used as foreign key in the statistics tables t03 and t05; likely the player id in an external source system.

col_003.name: player_name
col_003.description: Player's full name (e.g. 'Anthony Martial', 'Cristian Hidalgo'); some rows use short/nick names (e.g. 'Kiko', 'Paulinho').

col_004.name: player_alt_id
col_004.description: Another unique numeric identifier per player (range 2..234141), referenced by t05.col_002; purpose/origin unclear, possibly an id from a different source system.

col_005.name: birth_date
col_005.description: Player's date of birth (1967-1999 range, consistent with professional footballers).

col_006.name: height_cm
col_006.description: Player height in centimeters (157.48-208.28 cm; values are inch-to-cm conversions, e.g. 182.88 = 6 ft).

col_007.name: weight_kg
col_007.description: Player weight in kilograms (117-243 kg, mean ~168), consistent with footballer weights. The accepted joins to col_001 of t03/t05/t07 are likely coincidental numeric overlaps, not real references.

table.purpose: Per-ear hearing examination records (audiograms): each row is one ear's test with pure-tone hearing thresholds across many frequencies, linked to a patient/exam in t04 and measured on a date. The many 1–97 valued columns are consistent with hearing threshold levels in dB HL, and the left/right ear flag supports an audiology dataset (e.g. NHANES-style audiometry).

col_001.name: exam_id
col_001.description: Primary key of this table; sequential integer 1..183978 identifying one ear-level audiometric record. Referenced by t03, t04 and t07.

col_002.name: subject_id
col_002.description: Reference to t04.col_004; identifies the subject/patient (11,062 distinct, each appearing ~17 times on average, consistent with repeated visits and two ears per visit).

col_003.name: visit_id
col_003.description: Reference to t04.col_002; identifies the examination/visit. Distinct count (11,060) nearly equals col_002's, suggesting one visit per subject or a visit identifier of similar cardinality.

col_004.name: exam_date
col_004.description: Date of the hearing examination, ranging 2007-02-22 to 2016-07-07; the 2007-02-22 spike (11,794 rows) suggests a batch/backfill date.

col_005.name: age_at_baseline
col_005.description: Small integer 33–97, centered ~69. Consistently ~4–5 below col_006 in the same row; plausibly the subject's age at a baseline/reference visit (or age at first exam). Another reading: age at a related (earlier) measurement.

col_006.name: age_at_exam
col_006.description: Small integer 39–97, centered ~73.5; plausibly the subject's age at this exam. Always a few units above col_005, consistent with age at current visit vs baseline.

col_007.name: ear_side
col_007.description: Laterality of the tested ear: 'right' (138,409 rows) or 'left' (44,733 rows).

col_008.name: severity_category
col_008.description: Categorical with values medium/high/low plus dirty variants ('None', 'norm', 'stoc', 'le'); plausibly an overall hearing-loss severity grade, but the noisy values prevent certainty.

col_009.name: secondary_severity_category
col_009.description: Categorical dominated by medium/high/low with many noisy variants ('_0', digits, 'es', 'o'); likely another graded classification (e.g. severity in a different frequency band or a second rater's grade). Content is too corrupted to pin down.

table.name: football_clubs
table.purpose: Reference table of football (soccer) clubs, one row per club, with identifiers and the club's name and short code. Referenced by match/event data in t03 via multiple id columns.

col_001.name: club_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the club row. Unique integer identifier, referenced by many columns of t03 (each of those t03 columns apparently stores a club id, e.g. home/away or scorer/assisting player's club).

col_002.name: club_id_alt
col_002.description: Alternative unique club identifier, also referenced by t03 (col_008/col_009). Likely a second club key from another source (e.g. an external data-provider id). Distinct and unique like the primary key.

col_003.name: external_club_id
col_003.description: Another club identifier, mostly unique but with ~4% nulls and a few duplicates; range 1-112513 with a bimodal distribution (small ids and ~110k ids). Possibly a third-party id that is missing for some clubs; exact source unknown.

col_004.name: club_name
col_004.description: Full name of the football club (e.g. 'Siena', 'Hibernian', '1. FC Köln', 'Villarreal CF').

col_005.name: club_code
col_005.description: Three-letter abbreviation of the club name (e.g. SIE for Siena, CES for Cesena, HIB for Hibernian).

table.name: match_team_tactics
table.purpose: Per-match tactical setup and style ratings for a team in a football (soccer) match. Each row is one team's configuration for one match: two team identifiers, a season/match date, and pairs of (numeric rating 20-80, categorical label) describing playing style dimensions such as tempo, passing length, pressing, defensive line, width, etc. The vocabulary (Balanced/Fast/Slow, Short/Mixed/Long, Press/Contain/Double, Cover/Offside Trap, Deep/Medium/High) strongly suggests a football-management simulation dataset. The exact mapping of each rating/label pair to a specific tactical dimension is inferred from the label values and is therefore tentative for most columns.

col_001.name: tactic_id
col_001.description: Primary key; sequential surrogate id 1-1458, one per row (per team per match).

col_002.name: team_id
col_002.description: Identifier of one of the two teams in the match; references t05.col_001 (285 distinct teams, ~6 matches each).

col_003.name: opponent_team_id
col_003.description: Identifier of the opposing team in the same match; references t05.col_001 (288 distinct). Could alternatively be a match_id, but the value range and join to team tables suggest a team id.

col_004.name: season_date
col_004.description: Date with only 6 distinct values (Feb/Sep 2010-2015), each covering ~244 rows; looks like a season or season-start reference rather than an actual match date.

col_005.name: tempo_rating
col_005.description: Numeric style rating 20-80 paired with col_006 (Balanced/Fast/Slow), so likely the tempo/aggression of play.

col_006.name: tempo_label
col_006.description: Categorical counterpart of col_005: Balanced (81%), Fast, Slow — playing tempo.

col_009.name: passing_rating
col_009.description: Numeric rating 20-80 paired with col_010 (Short/Mixed/Long) — passing style/directness.

col_010.name: passing_label
col_010.description: Short/Mixed/Long — passing length/directness, counterpart of col_009.

col_011.name: structure_label
col_011.description: Organised (95%) vs Free Form; paired with col_012. Likely attacking/defensive structure discipline.

col_012.name: structure_rating
col_012.description: Numeric rating 21-80 paired with col_011 (Organised/Free Form).

col_013.name: risk_label
col_013.description: Normal/Risky/Safe, paired with col_014 — riskiness of play (e.g., tackling or passing risk).

col_018.name: structure_label_2
col_018.description: Organised/Free Form, paired with col_017; a second structure/discipline setting, distinct from col_011.

col_019.name: defensive_line_rating
col_019.description: Numeric rating 23-72 paired with col_020 (Deep/Medium/High) — defensive line height.

col_020.name: defensive_line_label
col_020.description: Medium (85%), Deep, High — defensive line height, counterpart of col_019.

col_021.name: pressing_rating
col_021.description: Numeric rating 24-72 paired with col_022 (Press/Double/Contain) — pressing style.

col_022.name: pressing_label
col_022.description: Press (87%), Double, Contain — pressing/defensive engagement style, counterpart of col_021.

col_023.name: width_rating
col_023.description: Numeric rating 29-73 paired with col_024 (Narrow/Normal/Wide) — attacking/defensive width.

col_024.name: width_label
col_024.description: Normal (88%), Wide, Narrow — width of play, counterpart of col_023.

col_025.name: offside_trap_setting
col_025.description: Cover (94%) vs Offside Trap — defensive strategy against through balls; whether the team plays the offside trap.
